hook.text: Oil and water don't mix—unless you force them. Mayonnaise is oil trapped in water by egg yolk chemistry.

buildup.text: An emulsion is a stable mixture of two liquids that normally separate. Milk, cream, and salad dressings are emulsions.

discovery.text: Lecithin in egg yolk is an emulsifier—one end loves water, the other loves fat. It bridges both worlds.

twist.text: Break the emulsion and mayonnaise splits into greasy soup. Temperature, speed, and ratio must be precise.

climax.text: Mustard is also an emulsifier. That's why vinaigrettes with mustard hold together longer than plain oil and vinegar.

punchline.text: Oil meets water. Add an emulsifier and they play nice.

quiz.question: What does an emulsifier do?
options: Bridges oil and water so they stay mixed
